LLM auditresponse for gulchce.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The script `gulchce.sh` is a wrapper used to manage user-specific runtime files for the GulchCE game. It creates a user directory under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/gulchce` (or `~/.local/share/gulchce`) and copies or updates the game binary (`halo`) from the system-wide installation in `/usr/lib/gulchce` only when the binary has changed (e.g., after a package update). This ensures each user runs a consistent version without requiring write access to the system directory.

The script establishes symbolic links to shared libraries (`libSDL3.so.0`) and configuration files (`brokers.txt`), allowing updates to be centrally managed while permitting user overrides (e.g., a user can replace the `brokers.txt` symlink with a regular file to customize it). A default `config.toml` is created if one does not exist, setting save paths and disabling the game's internal updater in favor of pacman-based updates—consistent with Arch packaging policies.

All operations are confined to the user's own data directory or involve safe, predictable use of standard Unix tools (`cp`, `mv`, `ln`, `printf`). There are no network operations, no use of `eval`, no execution of downloaded code, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or escalate privileges. The behavior aligns with standard AUR packaging practices for games that expect mutable per-user state alongside immutable system-wide binaries.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Safe wrapper managing per-user game state and updates</summary>
</security_assessment>
